'''David John Benney''' (8 April 1930 – 9 October 2015) was a New Zealand applied mathematician, known for work on the [[nonlinear partial differential equation]]s of [[fluid dynamics]].<ref name="MIT">{{cite web|url=https://math.mit.edu/about/history/obituaries/benney.php|title=David J. Benney, MIT Mathematics|work=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]|accessdate=7 January 2016}}</ref>{{sfn|Petersen|1971}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mathworld.wolfram.com/BenneyEquation.html|title=''Benney Equation'', Wolfram MathWorld|work=[[Wolfram Research]]|accessdate=7 January 2016}}</ref>

==Education and early life==
Born in [[Wellington]], New Zealand, on 8 April 1930 to [[Matt Benney|Cecil Henry (Matt) Benney]] and Phyllis Marjorie Jenkins,{{sfn|Petersen|1971|pp=84}} Benney was educated at [[Wellington College (New Zealand)|Wellington College]].<ref name="Bryant">{{cite journal |url=http://www.massey.ac.nz/~wwifs/mathnews/centrefolds/50/Dec1990.shtml |title=Professor David Benney |date=December 1990 | journal=NZMS Newsletter |first=Peter J. |last=Bryant |accessdate=5 March 2016}}</ref> He graduated BSc from [[Victoria University of Wellington|Victoria University College]] in 1950, and MSc from the same institution in 1951. He then went to [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]], from where he graduated BA in the [[Mathematical Tripos]] in 1954. He was at [[Canterbury University College]] for two years as a lecturer,<ref name="MIT"/> before taking leave of absence in August 1957 to undertake doctoral studies at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT), graduating PhD in 1959.<ref name="Bryant"/>

==Career and research==
Benney joined the mathematics faculty at MIT in 1960. He spent the rest of his career there, as a prolific researcher in fluid dynamics and supervisor of students, becoming [[emeritus professor]].<ref name="MIT"/> He received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1964.<ref>{{cite web|title=David J. Benney|url=http://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/david-j-benney/|website=John Simon Guggenheim Foundation|accessdate=12 July 2017}}</ref>
